newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan govt to buy land to boost liquidity - paper.
newsitem.headline: Japan govt to buy land to boost liquidity - paper.

text.p: The government plans to buy 380 billion yen worth of collateralised property previously owned by failed housing loan firms and other debt-ridden financial institutions in 1997/98 as part of measures to boost liquidity in Japan's property market, the business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Monday.
The purchase of collateralised land is expected to form a major part of the government's package of land liquidity measures due to be announced later on Monday.
The paper said the government will use public funds already allocated in the 1997/98 budget.

The land to be bought under the scheme will be used for social welfare facilities and parks, and is to also be developed in cooperation with the private sector for telecommunication facilities and other high-technology facilities, it said.
The government is considering purchasing a total of more than one trillion yen worth of collateralised land over the next three years to the end of 1999/2000, it added.

The Japan Development Bank, a government-affiliated financial institution, is expected to provide low-interest rate loans to finance facilities built on such land, the paper said. The Construction, Health and Welfare, and Posts and Telecommunications ministries will also provide subsidies, it added.
